The *Sulabha Sutta* ("Easy to Find", Iti 101; PTS It 102) is a discourse located in the fourth division (*Catukkanipāta*) of the *Itivuttaka*. The text expounds upon the four basic ascetic requisites, declaring that they are easy to obtain (*sulabha*) and blameless. According to the discourse, cultivating contentment with these four basic necessities constitutes a foundational factor of the contemplative life.

None of the retrieved secondary literature passages examine Iti 101 directly. Citations mentioning "Itivuttaka 101" in scholarship point instead to PTS page 101 (which contains the end of the preceding sutta, Iti 100), while other occurrences represent unrelated uses of the common adjective *sulabha* or the name of the epic philosopher Sulabhā.
